text:
on unit economics, this 2021 article "The Economics of Customer Businesses" from Mauboussin does a really good job laying out a bunch of frameworks that u can upload as industry-standard -- see the 4 screenshots below

these can fill an empty gap in "how should I think about all this," give u 3-5 different ways to do a revenue model, show u the deeper layers of price and volume and how to do everything on a per-unit basis

and then ties it into cogs/opex with CAC and LTV and churn and cohort analysis

u dont have to master all this immediately and it turns out to be more art than science, these are just frameworks and mental models to help understand how all the puzzle pieces fit together, the leads and lags of revenues and expenses in a business

this is a very common question which is why I bring it up ("how do I model revenue other than, like...revenue")

and this is all very "real-life" shit that u will spend days trying to model in various ways

like 5-10 tabs that aren't connected to the main financial statements, but are all coming at unit economics from different angles, in hopes that everything magically connects on its own

aka, u understand the business fluently

literally never happens

but a man's reach must exceed his grasp, or whats a heaven for?
